assessments.reasoning: Authenticity follows from publisher_pin at the Creative Commons legal-tools repository's fixed commit. Integrity follows from its matching [0,48) digest and whole-file SHA-256 a2010f343487d3f7618affe54f789f5487602331c0a8d03f49e9a7c547cf0499. Relevance follows from the title “Creative Commons Legal Code” and edition “CC0 1.0 Universal”. Interpretation is limited to identifying the material as legal-tool text. Applicability follows from the docs/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode.txt path at the same revision as publisher_readme. The contradiction check finds identical live plaintext and operative sections 1–4, ruling out a deed summary or image as the identified file. The title supplies descriptive context only.

Authenticity follows from publisher_readme at Creative Commons commit 91780e140892982eb3e0d530591ccbbca0d4690d. Integrity follows from the matching [10530,11678) digest covering both Copying and licenses and Trademark. Relevance follows from the publisher expressly dedicating its legal-tool text under CC0 1.0 Universal. Interpretation follows from that dedication read with publisher_pin section 1(i), which includes reproduction and distribution, and sections 2–3, which provide the waiver and fallback. Applicability follows from the same commit's English legalcode.txt being the very class of text named in the copying provision. The contradiction check finds a reservation for trademark and logo use in the cited range and distinct asset terms below it. Neither qualifies the stated copyright reuse of this file. The README supplies the operative authority.

limitations: The assessed copy retains the identified plaintext bytes. That condition bounds the claim and does not impose a general exact-copy requirement on CC0.
The README separately reserves Creative Commons trademarks and logos, subject to its stated exceptions. Other repository assets have their own terms.
A person's application of CC0 to another Work concerns that person's rights in that Work. It supplies no evidence that Creative Commons owns or clears those rights.
reasoning: Creative Commons' pinned README expressly dedicates “the text of the Creative Commons legal tools” under CC0 1.0 Universal. The same commit contains the identified English legal code as plaintext. Reproducing and redistributing its exact bytes falls within the copyright reuse covered by that dedication.
